The first step in our methodology, illustrated in Fig. 2 , is to map out the clinical workflow in which the medical device is intended to be deployed.

unlisted_practices: Map out the clinical workflow in which an AI device will be deployed, including other tools used alongside it, before hazard analysis.
Use structured hazard identification methods such as SHARD or HAZOP applied to the clinical and technical workflows, performed by a multidisciplinary team.
Use bow tie diagrams to visualise hazards, causes, consequences and risk controls and expose weak points needing new controls.
Develop a deployment safety case, a structured argument supported by evidence, that the AI system is safe in its clinical context.
Separate technical failures from clinical hazards in analysis to engage relevant expertise and improve communication between technical and clinical teams.
Compare deployment hazard analysis with the development hazard log to identify safety-relevant changes since development.
Estimate risk in terms of hazard probability and severity using a clinical focus rather than a purely technical perspective.

screen.reason: Evaluates and constructs a clinical safety case and hazard risk analysis based on real-world prospective deployment of the Paige prostate AI tool in UK hospitals.

primary.practice: deployment safety case and hazard/risk workflow analysis
